Summary: The paper proposes CertGate, a selective-prediction gate for multi-site clinical risk models that certifies, with confidence 1-delta, that an influence-weighted answered-set error rate (R_M) averaged over the population of sites is at most alpha, treating the site (hospital) rather than the record as the unit of independence. Each calibration site is collapsed into a bounded atom Z_c, a Waudby-Smith-Ramdas betting martingale tests E[Z] <= alpha, and a fixed-sequence (learn-then-test) walk over a threshold grid selects the operating point. Two assumption modes are offered: an exchangeable baseline and a BBSE label-shift mode whose four estimated parameters carry cluster-bootstrap/Clopper-Pearson uncertainty into the budget. A linear head supplies exact additive attributions for answers and abstentions, plus a three-way answered-set composition disclosure. Experiments on a 208-site synthetic cohort (E1-E7, incl. a verified concept-shift negative control and a record-as-unit comparator) and on eICU-CRD v2.0 (164,322 stays, 207 hospitals, protocol frozen before the extract was read) show alpha=0.10 certifies at ~0.98 (synthetic) and 0.89 (eICU) coverage while alpha=0.05 is unreachable at this site count; the BBSE mode declines essentially everywhere.
Strengths: Correct and clearly stated estimand: the site-population-average influence-weighted answered-set risk, with the site as the unit of independence; the guarantee text explicitly disclaims per-site bounds, realized counts, and concept shift, which is unusually careful.

The certification core is sound: bounded per-site atoms feed a WSR betting supermartingale, validity follows from Ville's inequality, and the fixed-sequence walk over the threshold grid avoids delta-splitting; the equivalence E[Z] <= alpha iff R_M <= alpha is straightforward and correct.

Validation design includes elements many papers omit: a negative control verified capable of failing (E3), a record-as-unit comparator on identical draws (E7), a sensitivity sweep of the one influential constant (E4.9), and a real-data application with a protocol and constants pinned before the extract was read, with attrition ledger, leak screens, an external clinical comparator, and pre-declared predictions that were scored (four confirmed, three falsified).

Honest disclosure of the gate's cost on real data: answered-set mortality 0.046 vs 0.090 in the pool, negative answered-minus-all skill contrast, per-hospital answered error up to 0.29 under a valid certificate.
Full code release with deterministic, byte-identical regeneration of the synthetic grid; the eICU pipeline is reproducible by any credentialed holder.
Weaknesses: Methodological novelty is thin for an ML venue: the certificate is learn-then-test with WSR betting p-values (already the construction in Angelopoulos et al.'s LTT) applied to cluster-level bounded atoms, plus a BBSE box following Si et al. The influence weight g_c = min(n_c, M) and the atom linearization are minor. The paper is essentially an engineering instantiation of known tools with careful reporting.

The empirical validity evidence never tests the certificate where it could fail: in E1 the realized fresh-pool R_M is ~0.057 against alpha=0.10 (and 0.048 vs 0.10 on eICU), so 0/200 exceedances says nothing about the actual level of the test at delta. There is no boundary experiment where the true R_M sits near alpha; the only failures shown are under violated assumptions (E2 baseline, E3).

The certified rung is close to trivial at the working prevalence: the paper itself notes an always-negative rule errs at ~0.104 (synthetic) and the eICU target-pool prevalence is 0.0898 < alpha = 0.10, and the gate lowers answered mortality by abstaining where deaths concentrate. The alpha=0.05 rung that would be informative is unreachable below ~300-400 sites, and the BBSE mode certifies 0/200 at the anchor shift, 9% at null shift, and nothing on eICU. Net: at realistic multi-site scales the method certifies only a budget a trivial predictor nearly meets, and the label-shift contribution is demonstrated only as a refuser.

The certified quantity is arguably not what a deployer needs: a site-population average of a symmetric 0-1 loss where ~77% of answered errors are false negatives; a single hospital ran at 0.29 answered error under a valid certificate; sensitivity/FNR are not bounded. The choice M=100 (site-equal weighting) is what makes certification feasible (at M=5000, i.e., record-proportional error, nothing certifies), so feasibility is purchased by changing the estimand.

No comparison against simpler cluster-level valid alternatives (cluster Hoeffding / empirical-Bernstein CIs on Z_c, cluster bootstrap, hierarchical conformal risk control adapted to selective risk), so it is unclear what the betting martingale buys. E7 scores the record-unit comparator against the site-weighted R_M it never claimed, and at s_u=0.5 its violation rate (3.5%) is actually below delta; the motivating failure is only shown clearly in one heterogeneity arm at one rung, on a 2,000-record subsample chosen without justification.

The BBSE mode is not finite-sample (three of four intervals are percentile bootstraps with measured joint miscoverage 0.038 vs nominal <= 0.019), yet the abstract and title advertise finite-sample confidence without qualification; the mode also requires >= 10 declared target sites and declines for 2-9, limiting applicability.

Synthetic generator is very simple (8 features, linear signal, logistic head well-specified to the generator; heterogeneity only via a random intercept), and no non-linear head is run despite the 'model-agnostic' claim. The explainability contribution amounts to w_j(x_j - mu_j) attributions for a linear model and a margin-to-answer scalar; E5 returns a null and the eICU driver reading is unvalidated clinically.

Presentation: dense, idiosyncratic prose with heavy self-characterization ('honest', 'deliberately', 'load-bearing'), paragraph-length table captions, and spurious 6-decimal precision (e.g., ECE 0.002914, skill margin 0.003934); the abstract's Results paragraph is a wall of numbers. Related work omits group-conditional / multivalid risk-control lines that offer per-group guarantees, and selective-classification disparity work relevant to the composition disclosure.
Questions: Boundary validity: please add a synthetic configuration where the true R_M at the deployed threshold sits at or just below alpha and report the realized certify-and-exceed rate against delta; E1's 0/200 at R_M ~ 0.057 vs alpha = 0.10 is uninformative about the test's actual level.

E7: what are the record-unit comparator's violation rates when scored against the record-proportional answered error on the fresh pool (the estimand it actually claims), and with the full S_cal rather than a 2,000-record subsample?

How does the betting martingale compare, in certified coverage and threshold, to a cluster-level empirical-Bernstein or Hoeffding confidence bound on Z_c, or a cluster bootstrap, at 74-83 calibration clusters?

Would a constant always-negative rule (full coverage, R_M ~ 0.09) certify at alpha = 0.10 on eICU with 74 calibration clusters? If it comes close, what does the certificate tell a deployer beyond what prevalence alone implies?
Is there any realistic configuration (multi-site target pool, moderate shift) in which the BBSE mode certifies a non-trivial fraction of draws? What target-pool size and site count would it take?

For eICU: what is the index/prediction time and feature window, and how are stays that end (including by death) before the window closes handled? Are any features observable only after the prediction time?
Please run a non-linear head (e.g., gradient boosting) through the pipeline to substantiate the model-agnostic claim and show the certified coverage trade-off.
What is the basis for the 50 record-carrying-calibration-cluster minimum and the 10-record answerable floor, and how sensitive are E4 and the eICU per-hospital arm to them?
Given the bootstrap intervals in the BBSE box are asymptotic, will the abstract and guarantee text qualify the 'finite-sample' claim to the exchangeable mode only?
Limitations: The authors are unusually thorough about limitations (site-average scope, no per-site bound, concept shift excluded, temporal common shocks unmodeled, symmetric loss, single real cohort, asymptotic BBSE intervals). Additional points worth stating explicitly: (i) at typical multi-site scales (well under 150 hospitals) the method cannot certify any rung, which sharply limits practical applicability; (ii) the certificate does not bound sensitivity or false-negative rate, which is what mortality triage cares about, and abstention concentrates on the sickest patients, shifting workload and risk to deferral; (iii) a 'certificate' banner risks over-trust at an individual hospital despite the site-average scope, as the 0.29 answered-error hospital illustrates; (iv) 3,996 cross-hospital patients are left in, so site-disjointness is only approximate.
Potential negative societal impact is modest and mostly addressed; the main risk is misuse of a population-average certificate as a per-site or per-patient safety claim.
